correctness.rationale: The rechecked result uses the cofactor identity to give z²+uz+conj(u) and D²=|u²−4conj(u)|. Since |u|≤1, the unique discriminant root is the weight barycenter. Modding out the normals by one global phase or sign gives respectively a two-torus or four planes at that point, and diagonal phases/signs commute with A. The Frobenius identity gives norm one at the barycenter, so this is a nonzero nilpotent, not a scalar. Schur triangle eigenvector overlap ν/√(ν²+D²) gives unit-column κ=(√(ν²+D²)+ν)/D, with ν²=1+(|u|²−D²)/2. Compactness excludes other tail contributions. Near zero, D∼2√|u| and κ∼|u|^(−1/2); the affine Jacobian 3√3/2 and Dirichlet weights give center densities 4/(3√3), 1/π. Disks of radii asymptotic to ε²/4 and R^(−2) give the four constants, and the positive R^(−4) tail via layer cake proves the p<4 cutoff including divergence at p=4. Independent script /workspace/branches/d316504f-57b8-4fb1-ad94-dd09de05eafe/independent_check.py and independent_check.txt there give 372 exact barycentric checks and 1,000 direct assertions across 200 planes, including center nilpotence and the conditioning formula. Limits are analytic, not fitted.

Malamud characterizes which spectra can arise in codimension one. The workshop document poses randomized Ritz-distribution questions. The Carden–Hansen abstract describes geometric constraints for pairs of Ritz values in dimension three, but the full text was unavailable.

value.rationale: The smallest nontrivial orthogonal compression of a symmetric three-level unitary spectrum is a concrete benchmark for nonnormal behavior from a fixed normal input. Almost-sure simplicity conceals a precise fourth-moment obstruction; comparing real and complex trial planes at the same input isolates distinct quantitative constants. The simultaneous gap and unit-vector conditioning laws give more information than the feasible Ritz region or generic warning about near-defectiveness.
